question: Which producers must LEGITIMATELY stay on the muon anchor, and must NOT be re-pinned to proton by a consumer sweep?
asked_by: PR #5765 comment on PR #5500: 'which producers have you already established must legitimately stay muon (anchor-defining / dual-layer / deliberate comparison) — I'd rather inherit your list than rebuild it'

method.candidates: regex over every computations/**/*.py (excluding _deprecated): an assert on a q0 prefix literal, a raise/SystemExit mentioning muon, or prose saying a muon run is required
method.verdicts: AGENT-CONFIRMED by reading each candidate. The regex is high-recall: 4 of 8 undeclared candidates were FALSE POSITIVES and are listed under rejected[] with the reason, so a re-run does not re-litigate them.
method.scope_note: This answers 'must stay muon', which is NOT the same question as 'is stamped muon' (78) or 'carries the muon value' (139). See q0_muon_population_partition.py --list for those.

anchor_defining.rule: AGENTS.md STRICT: never re-pin as if it were a consumer. It DEFINES the muon anchor; re-pinning it collapses both anchors, flips every correctly-stamped muon witness, and hard-fails every ideal_muon producer including this one. Broke main once; recovery + ANCHOR_DEFINING exclusion list in 2e4745448d.

members.note: The ONE file PR #5500 legitimately changes — as the anchor's own re-derivation, never as part of a consumer sweep.

refuses_non_muon_run.rule: The producer raises rather than run at the proton pin. A sweep that re-pins it does not migrate it; it breaks it.

members.note: ALSO dual-layer: emits one witness per layer via --anchor. Its error text mislabels the muon value as 'the PROTON pin' — wrong either way, still open.

asserts_anchor_prefix.rule: Reads q from the anchor-defining witness and asserts its prefix. These must move WITH the anchor (A->C), never to proton. PR #5500 updates all four asserts.

members.GAP: Asserts the anchor prefix but is absent from q0_anchor_manifest.json. It is a muon consumer that the manifest cannot see, so QOU_Q0_ANCHOR does not reach it. Reported, NOT fixed here — a manifest edit is the migration's own change (AGENTS.md constraint 4: do not split it).

dual_layer.rule: Anchor-parameterised: emits one artifact per layer. Needs BOTH pins; the manifest cannot express that, so it is served per-process. DETECTION (added 2026-08-29): a producer emitting two witnesses whose `q0Anchor` values DIFFER is dual-layer by construction. That test found 4 where the originating regex -- which keys on assertions, raises and prose -- had found 2, because a producer that simply writes both layers makes no assertion and raises nothing.

resolves_muon_as_reference.rule: Does NOT compute at the muon pin — it RESOLVES the pin to measure other things against. Never re-pin these; but note their OUTPUTS move when the anchor moves, so they need re-running as part of the migration, not exclusion from it.

co_readers_cannot_be_repointed_alone.rule: Reads a SECOND field of the anchor witness besides q, so re-pointing only the q read would straddle two layers inside one quantity — which AGENTS.md forbids outright. Migrate whole or not at all.

derives_the_muon_pin.rule: DERIVES the muon pin from its own definition -- the CAL-2 lepton tower `m_mu/m_e = Vol(4_1)/hbar_q^2`, `hbar_q = 1 - q0^-1`, inverted as `q0 = 1/(1 - sqrt(Vol_4_1 / M_MU_OVER_M_E))`. These do not READ an anchor; they COMPUTE one, and the one they compute is the ideal/CAL-2 layer. Re-pinning them to proton is incoherent: the quantity they produce IS the muon-anchored one, so a proton stamp would describe a number that does not exist in the file. DETECTION: `M_MU_OVER_M_E` (or `codata_2022_source`) imported AND `hbar_q` present AND a `q0 = .../(1 - hbar_q)` assignment. The mass-ratio import alone OVER-MATCHES -- `rho_k_h3a_residual_decomposition` imports muon material but has hbar_q nowhere; it uses the muon value as an explicit comparison reference, which is a different class. Added 2026-08-29 (qou-cds3).

derives_the_muon_pin.note: Found while partitioning the INDIRECT remainder. A marker scan for q0 names (q_muon_at, pin_value_for_anchor, the anchor witness, a muon literal, QOU_Q0_ANCHOR) reports NO muon route for these, and an upstream scan reports none either -- because the route is neither a q0 name nor a witness read, but a mass ratio. That is why the class was missing. Corroborated independently: three of these six (t6_tau_h5_embedding_probe, t6_three_halves_factor_probes, xi_ell_phi_q_probe) are exactly the witnesses that flipped proton -> muon in the PR #5989 drain, where `resolve_q0_anchor_payload_first` caught them declaring proton (the manifest default for an unlisted stem) over a muon computation. The two findings explain each other.
